subject.title: Memory system: Cannot delete stale memories, conflicting entries persist

question: Should `memory_recall` expose deletable UUIDs in model-visible content now, or should all correction and conflict handling wait for the broader memory lifecycle design?
rationale: Source and live evidence show a real deletion-handoff gap, but changing visible tool output, accepting recall indexes, or adding supersede semantics defines user-visible memory tool behavior.

options.title: Expose UUIDs in recall output
options.body: Ship a narrow additive change so recalled memories can be passed directly to `memory_forget(memoryId=...)`, while keeping replacement/deprecation out of scope.

options.title: Accept recall indexes in forget
options.body: Map visible recall indexes to memories, but only after defining session state, ambiguity, and stale-result rules.

options.title: Defer to memory MVP
options.body: Keep this issue as input to the broader review/edit/forget/conflict-resolution design and avoid a narrower tool-output contract for now.

recommendation.title: Expose UUIDs in recall output
recommendation.body: Ship a narrow additive change so recalled memories can be passed directly to `memory_forget(memoryId=...)`, while keeping replacement/deprecation out of scope.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent memory-lancedb and review history makes this the best available routing candidate for the tool-output/product-boundary choice.
